name: Dreams Natura Resort & Spa

kids_club.evidence: Explorer's Club takes potty-trained 3-12s at no charge and parents of preschoolers praise it, but the only published hours (10am-6pm) date from 2020 and current hours are unverified.

water_play.evidence: Free on-site water park with a lazy river and three big slides (reported 1.20 m minimum height, so likely too tall for young children), plus a separate kids' water area with spray jets, four mini slides and a tipping bucket.

beach.evidence: The beach sits on the open coast between Cancun and Puerto Morelos, not in Costa Mujeres; several reviews describe heaped sargassum, brownish water and little ocean swimming. Sargassum season usually builds through late April, and April 2026 set regional records.

rooms.evidence: Junior suites come with two double beds or a king plus sofa bed, and a Family Junior Suite with connecting rooms is offered; 553 rooms in total.

food.evidence: Nine venues including Italian, seafood, Pan-Asian/hibachi, Mexican and a steakhouse, but the French restaurant is 16+ and several reviewers say the booking system fills fast and tables are hard to get.

transfer.evidence: About 16 km from CUN; sources put the drive at roughly 15-30 minutes.

condition.evidence: Opened in 2020 (rebranded from Now Natura before opening), so it is fairly new, but 2025-26 reviews mention musty rooms, AC and hot-water faults and worn fixtures.

kids_club.name: Explorer's Club
kids_club.notes: Must be potty-trained. Separate Core Zone teen club. Recent parents of 3-4 year olds rate the staff highly.

pros: Kids' splash area with mini slides and a bucket, plus a lazy river, all included
Two-double-bed suites and connecting family suites
Wide cuisine variety: Italian, seafood, Pan-Asian, Mexican
cons: Beach is regularly hit by heavy sargassum, and the ocean is often not swimmable
Big water slides likely need 1.20 m height, so young children may be limited to the kids' area
Kids' club hours reported as 10am-6pm (old data), so evenings are on the parents
À la carte reservations are hard to get, according to several reviewers
Not actually in Costa Mujeres: it is on the Puerto Morelos stretch of coast south of Cancun
verdict: Great pools and a short transfer for young children, but plan the week around the water park rather than the sea, because the beach is one of the area's worst for sargassum.
